editorial:
Imagine a guy who believes every single word of the Bible and thinks the world is full of sin. Now, put him right in the middle of Panama City, Florida, during the peak of spring break. You get a wild setup where a strict religious man walks through crowds of partying college kids and people in bikinis. The whole vibe is awkward and tense because he is completely out of place. It feels like a social experiment where you just wait to see when someone is finally going to snap. 

What really works here is how the movie makes you feel the heat and the noise of the beach. The acting is solid, and the slow build-up makes the ending feel earned. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you want a big action movie, but it is great if you like character studies. You should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you love rare films, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up when the main character finally hits his breaking point with the chaos around him. After spending the whole film judging everyone, he has a sudden realization that his anger is the real problem. He stops preaching and simply walks away from the crowd, leaving his Bible behind on the sand. It is a quiet ending that shows he has finally let go of his hate and found some peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange character studies and indie films.
